function.mechanism: Acts as a sulfiting agent; in aqueous/acidic foods it generates sulfite/bisulfite/sulfur dioxide species that reduce oxidation and inhibit browning and some microbial growth.

adi.basis: EFSA follow-up (2022) withdrew the temporary group ADI because the toxicity database was inadequate; 2016 had set a temporary group ADI of 0.7 mg SO2 equivalents/kg bw/day.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA found unresolved data gaps, withdrew the temporary ADI, and reported MOE-based safety concern for several population groups/exposure scenarios.

adi.basis: Group ADI for sulfites listed as 0-0.7 mg/kg bw/day (includes metabisulfites).

concerns.summary: EFSA 2022 used prolonged visual evoked potential latency as a critical endpoint (BMDL 38 mg SO2 eq/kg bw/day) and found MOE concerns at estimated dietary exposures.
Sulfite hypersensitivity is documented in susceptible individuals; a DBPC case report identified anaphylaxis to potassium metabisulfite.
key_references: Clonal mast cell activation syndrome with anaphylaxis to sulfites (PMID 23816954)

concerns.summary: A study reported dose-dependent chromosome aberrations, SCE, and micronuclei effects in human lymphocytes and rat bone marrow at high experimental doses.
A recent large prospective cohort found associations between several preservatives, including potassium metabisulfite, and higher type 2 diabetes incidence; causality not established.

no_concern_confirmed: IARC classification list places sulfur dioxide/bisulfites/metabisulfites in Group 3 (not classifiable for carcinogenicity to humans).
A CIU challenge study reported additive sensitivity (including potassium metabisulfite among tested additives) to be <1% in that cohort.

populations: some adult and elderly subgroups under specific scenarios
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA and JECFA exposure assessments report potential exceedance/insufficient MOE in several scenarios and subpopulations.

risk_assessment.rationale: Using the provided tier rules, EFSA's 2022 inability to retain an ADI and explicit MOE-based safety concern outweigh historical approval status.
key_factors: EFSA 2022 withdrew temporary ADI and identified safety concern
Exposure concern signals in high consumers and younger populations
Documented sulfite hypersensitivity in susceptible individuals
No IARC carcinogenic signal above Group 3 and no broad jurisdictional ban
